Definition: of Hebrew origin (H7343); Raab (i.e. Rachab), a Canaanitess:--Rahab. See also G4477.
BiblicalUsage: By faith the harlot Rahab perished not with them that believed not, when she had received the spies with peace, and James asks whether she was not justified by works when she had received the messengers and sent them out another way. She hid the spies on her roof and let them down by the scarlet cord, and her house was spared when the wall fell.
TheologicalSignificance: What I take from this is that Rahab is in the story because faith takes the spies in and works sends them out, and God counts both.
